Messages.Author: self biased
Messages.Body:
I have a vampire in combat and I play Skin of night. ( This vampire treats aggravated damage as normal damage for the remainder of this round.
As above, and prevent 1 damage.) later in the round, that vampire takes 3 Aggravated damage. Can I use Soak ( Prevent 2 non-aggravated damage.
Prevent 4 non-aggravated damage.) or other cards that specifically prevent non-aggravated damage as my vampire treats them as normal damage?

Messages.Author: Malachy
Messages.Body:
> Can I use Soak ( Prevent 2 non-aggravated damage.
> Prevent 4 non-aggravated damage.) or other cards that specifically prevent non-aggravated damage as my vampire treats them as normal damage?
>
Nope.

The damage is still considered aggravated whether your vampire treat it as normal damage or not!

NC of Hungary

///

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> Malachy wrote:
> The damage is still considered aggravated whether your vampire treat it as normal damage or not!
>
Confirmed in  [LSJ 20001223]

> LSJ wrote:
> > Skin of night allows to treat agg gamage like normal. So, can I play it
> > and then play Superior Resillence to prevent 3 agg damage?
>
> No. Superior Resilience will only prevent normal (non-agg) damage.
> Skin of Night allows you to treat the damage as normal (that is,
> you can burn a blood to heal it and it won't burn you if your
> wounded), but the damage is still aggravated.
>

Messages.Author: AaronC
Messages.Body:
Yes, if you read French: www.veknfrance.com/forum/viewtopic.php?t=16154

The same answer is given (in French) under the Skin of Night entry as well as an active link to the same ruling.

Pierre Van Tran created this excellent reference page. Even if you don't speak French, you might find the links under the different card names to be useful since they lead to relevant rulings. It is close to complete, although I think it may be missing some very recent rulings or non-card specific rulings.

A couple of years ago I translated T-Z into English and submitted them to Pascal. (I'm a native English-speaker who speaks French decently well.) Besides a 'thank you', he didn't suggest that I continue or indicate how he might use the translations. I might be interested in continuing that work if there were a public forum for it.

Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body:
I am converting that French list into an English database. Hoepfully, the whole process will make judging way easier.

Regarding the OP's question, Malachy and jamesatzephyr's answers are correct. Also notice: there are no longer cards that change the nature of damage (all were reworded to read "treat as")
